thread:
oscar: Noting a customer report: Console role autocomplete (when adding a binding) is suggesting roles from other tenants. Potential data leak. Repro: open Roles > Add binding > type `billing` -> suggestions include `acme:BillingAdmin` and `global:BillingViewer` even though I'm scoped to tenant:zephyr.
oscar: customer screenshot attached shows role name + tenant in suggestion list which is a privacy issue.
lydia: yikes. Which endpoint does the UI call for suggestions?
oscar: UI calls `GET /api/v1/roles/autocomplete?q=billing&scope=tenant:zephyr&limit=10` and the response includes names with scopes that don't match the supplied scope param. Sample response snippet:
```json
{"suggestions":[{"id":"r_201","name":"BillingAdmin","scope":"tenant:acme"},{"id":"r_202","name":"TenantBilling","scope":"tenant:zephyr"}]}
```
ben: quick question: are we leaking role names only or full role metadata? If it's just display names that's still bad but easier to fix.
oscar: currently we return `id,name,scope,description` for suggestions. Customer example had description text that included internal notes.
priya: immediate mitigation: 1) UI change - hide scope and description in the suggestion dropdown for canary tenants and show `Only showing tenant-scoped roles` hint; 2) backend change - make autocomplete honor scope param strictly and drop global matches unless `include_global=true` is explicit and caller has entitlement.
ben: digging in - index query uses a shared `role_search_view` that contains normalized tokens across tenants. The autocomplete query uses `fuzzy_match` and then does a join to roles but we accidentally removed the scope WHERE clause in the refactor for perf. So index returns candidates across tenants and join later filters are optimized away by planner on PG due to a bad subquery shape.
priya: can we patch quick: wrap scope filter into the primary index predicate instead of a WHERE on outer query so planner can't drop it? Also add a `tenant_id` equality column to the indexed expression.
oscar: agreed. Also add a strict check in the HTTP layer: if response contains suggestions with scope != requested scope and tenant is not admin, return 403-guarded empty list and log an incident. That buys time for index fix.
search-bot: alert: potential PII exposure in autocomplete - creating incident ticket #INC-9342.
lydia: telemetry: emit `perm_autocomplete.scope_violation` with count + tenant + request_id. We need to know how many users hit this before the fix.
priya: PR plan: services/search/autocomplete.go -> enforce scope param in index predicate, add a fast-path that returns tenant-only suggestions for non-admins; add unit tests for admin/non-admin callers; add integration test that simulates planner dropping predicate. Also add migration to add `tenant_token` to GIN index expression used by fuzzy_match.
ben: for UI: hide scope/description by default for suggestions and add a tiny warning banner in the Add Binding modal: "Autocompletion is temporarily restricted while we fix a bug" behind flag `hideRoleSuggestionDetails`.
oscar: ops ask: throttle autocomplete endpoints per-tenant while we patch to reduce blast radius. Add rate limit `100 req/min` per tenant and emit `perm_autocomplete.rate_limited` in telemetry.
sre-bot: scheduled: page on-call if `perm_autocomplete.scope_violation` > 5/min for > 10 minutes.
deploy-bot: staging deploy queued (build #9401) - running unit tests.
priya: I'll include rollback notes: if the index change causes slowdowns revert to HTTP-layer filtering + UI hide. Also add a backfill job to reindex `role_search_view` with tenant_token expression.
lydia: postmortem checklist: 1) notify affected customers with timeline & remediation steps; 2) audit logs for all role suggestions returned in last 24h for tenants with violations; 3) add an automated test to the CI that asserts `GET /roles/autocomplete?scope=tenant:X` never returns suggestions with other scopes.
oscar: thanks. I'll start the hotfix PR and coordinate customer notifications with support.
